title: Forensic Readiness & Key Rotation PRD — SSO/RBAC/KMS Acceptance Plan
creator: Aria Patel
description: Objective: Define requirements, acceptance criteria, and a sign-off checklist to make Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) ‘forensics-ready’ while enabling safe KMS/HSM key rotation and preserving SSO/RBAC controls and auditable trails. This PRD clarifies scope changes requested by Compliance and Ops after initial crypto spec review and consolidates the acceptance plan for stakeholders to sign off prior to release.
background: Compliance and enterprise customers requested two gaps be closed before wide Private rollout: (1) proofable, non-destructive key rotation with an HSM-backed key hierarchy and zero downtime fallback; (2) deterministic, tamper-evident audit trails that link SSO identity, RBAC decision, and KMS operations for forensic investigations. Early design (crypto v1) covered KMS integration but lacked rotation runbooks and explicit forensic fields in logs. This ticket bridges that gap and collects cross-functional signoffs.
sso_saml_rbac_requirements: SAML 2.0 IdP integration with SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows; fallback to local accounts only where explicitly enabled by admin
SCIM v2 provisioning support for groups and user lifecycle; record provisioning events (create/update/deactivate) in audit logs
RBAC primitives: OrgOwner, OrgAdmin, InfraAdmin, AuditReader, Developer. Minimum privilege principle enforced by default roles and ability to create custom roles
Authorization decision logs must include: actor_sso_id, sso_assertion_id, evaluated_permissions_set, resource_path, decision (allow/deny), request_id, timestamp
Admin UI and API must display role-change diffs and require two-step approval for InfraAdmin assignments (owner + security approver) in high-compliance tenants
kms_hsm_requirements: Support for external HSMs (PKCS#11) and cloud-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) via an abstraction layer
A customer master key (CMK) rotation flow: schedule-based rotation with optional manual trigger; rotation should produce new key material while maintaining ability to decrypt historical ciphertexts
All envelope encryption done with DEKs stored encrypted under CMKs; no plaintext CMKs stored in the application
Key usage audit events: key_create, key_rotate_start, key_rotate_complete, key_disable, key_schedule_delete, key_export_attempt (always denied and logged)
Rotation must be HSM-backed where customer selected HSM integration; rotation operations must require InfraAdmin RBAC permission plus a separate key-rotation approval flag for high-security tenants
audit_log_requirements: Immutable append-only log architecture with tamper-evidence markers (hash chaining) per-tenant for at least 7 years retention in Private deployments

Audit entries must include: timestamp (RFC3339), request_id, actor_type (user/service), actor_sso_id, actor_ip, action, resource, outcome, request_payload_digest, response_digest, pre_state_digest (where applicable)
Support export of filtered audit slices for compliance/supervisory review (CSV/NDJSON) and cryptographic proof (signed manifest) for delivered exports
Alerting on suspicious audit patterns (bulk deletes, repeated failed auth attempts, cross-region key access) and automated preservation hold for affected tenants
Audit read access controlled by RBAC; AuditReader can view but not delete or export beyond configured tenant policies
acceptance_criteria: Automated key rotation completes without service downtime in a staging Private deployment: rotate CMK, ensure all new DEKs are encrypted under new CMK, and verify decryption of objects encrypted under previous CMKs
Audit trail for a simulated incident (SSO login -> role-change -> key-rotation -> attempted secret export) reconstructs end-to-end chain with request_ids and verifies hash-chain integrity
RBAC enforcement blocks unauthorized key rotation or export attempts; corresponding authorization decision logs recorded and match the actor SSO assertion
Exported audit slices include signed manifests that allow verification of completeness and integrity using our public verification tool
HSM-backed rotation path exercised with an HSM emulator in staging and validated by Crypto team: no plaintext key material is recoverable from service memory after rotation

scope_changes: Added: cryptographic export-proof manifests for audit exports after Compliance requested verifiable delivery
Added: explicit tamper-evidence hash-chaining requirement for Private deployments (not required in hosted initially)
Removed: automatic cross-region key mirroring for first release (deferred to runtime-1.20) to reduce blast radius and simplify verification
Clarified: local account fallback is opt-in and must be logged as a high-risk configuration
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (staging-only): implement rotation + audit log enrichment; smoke tests for decryption of legacy objects
Stage 2 (internal canary): enable on internal Private tenant with SRE and Security on-call; apply simulated incident playbook
Stage 3 (customer pilot): 2 enterprise customers opt-in with contractual acceptance; run on-demand Q/A with Compliance teams
Stage 4 (general availability): enable on Private customers with release notes, runbooks, and migration tools (if needed)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Key rotation could inadvertently make older data unreadable if DEK re-wrapping fails. Mitigation: transactional rotation with pre-rotation snapshot and automated rollback path; verification step marks rotation complete only after sample reads succeed
Risk: Audit/export interfaces may leak PII if filters misconfigured. Mitigation: export guardrails and masking defaults; Compliance sign-off required for any export enabling PII fields
Risk: HSM integration increases deployment complexity. Mitigation: provide an HSM emulator and hardened runbooks; defer advanced features (cross-region mirroring) to later releases
open_questions: What SLA do we commit to for rotation completion time in tight latency-sensitive tenants? (Security and SRE to propose limits)
Does compliance require independent archival of signed manifests to a customer's archive location? (Legal/Compliance input needed)
Should we provide a forensic toolkit (local verifier) bundled in the Private deployment or as a separate binary?
decisions: Decision: Maintain envelope encryption pattern; CMKs never leave HSM or KMS boundary in clear text
Decision: Implement per-tenant hash-chaining for logs rather than a global chain to simplify integrity proofs and privacy isolation
Decision: Two-step approval required for InfraAdmin role assignments in high-compliance tenants
test_plan_high_level: Unit tests for audit event schema and signing of export manifests
Integration tests for SAML sign-on -> SCIM provisioning -> RBAC assignment -> audit traceability
End-to-end rotation test in staging with HSM emulator including rollback simulation
Chaos test: simulate partial rotation failure and verify rollback completes and notifies stakeholders
monitoring_and_alerting: Rotation failures and partial-rotation states emit PagerDuty alerts to SRE and Security
Audit-chain integrity alerts on detection of hash breaks or missing entries
Unauthorized key access attempts increase a severity metric and trigger preservation hold on related tenant logs
